contributions.anchor: Box B 'Contributions Received this Period' (1,687.48) on the p5 Summary Page, which is also Schedule A's own printed 'Subtotal for this page' (1,687.48) AND its printed 'Total Contributions Received — Sum of all Schedule A pages in this report' (1,687.48)
contributions.detail: The 4 Schedule A rows on p2 sum to 653.32 + 109.16 + 25.00 + 900.00 = 1,687.48 exactly, equal to all three printed figures; the page-subtotal gate and the sum-of-all-pages gate coincide because Schedule A is a single sheet. THE TWO SELF-LOANS ARE INSIDE THE ANCHOR: rows 1 and 2 are 'Aaron Davidson (Loan)' 653.32 and 109.16, written on the contributions ledger, and the filer's own subtotal includes them — running the ladder (ADDENDUM B3) makes them ITEMIZED CONTRIBUTION ROWS, not beginning-balance items, and Box A is a printed 0.00 so there is no beginning-balance slot for them in any case. Box C 'Contributions Received Year to Date' prints 1,687.48 and is CUMULATIVE: it equals Box B here only because this is the filer's FIRST report of the cycle, which is not an anomaly.

expenditures.anchor: Box D 'Expenditures Made this Period' (959.45) on the p5 Summary Page, which is also the figure printed as 'Total Expenditures Made — Sum of all Schedule B pages in this report' on both Schedule B sheets; the per-sheet gates are the printed 'Subtotal for this page' figures 879.14 (p3) and 80.31 (p4)
expenditures.detail: Two Schedule B sheets, 20 rows. p3's 15 rows sum to 653.32 + 9.16 + 58.99 + 0.57 + 38.34 + 11.70 + 4.68 + 11.70 + 9.36 + 21.06 + 11.12 + 11.70 + 12.87 + 15.21 + 9.36 = 879.14 = its printed subtotal. p4's 5 rows sum to 1.17 + 28.08 + 15.21 + 5.85 + 30 = 80.31 = its printed subtotal. The two subtotals sum to 959.45, equal to the schedule's own sum-of-all-pages total AND to Box D. Every mileage row also reproduces the filer's own printed rate (miles x .585, which he prints inside each Purpose cell): 20->11.70, 8->4.68, 16->9.36, 36->21.06, 19->11.12, 22->12.87, 26->15.21, 2->1.17, 48->28.08, 10->5.85 — an independent per-row check that the whole column is read correctly, and it is CLEAN on this filing (contrast his November filing, where exactly one such row breaks the rule and produces a +0.09 delta). Box E 'Expenditures Made Year to Date' prints 959.45 and is CUMULATIVE, equal to Box D only because this is his first report. The summary ladder is internally consistent: Box F 1,687.48 = Box A 0.00 + Box B 1,687.48, and the close 728.03 = Box F - Box D 959.45.

itemized.in_kind_convention: monetary-only, and BOTH sides close on it exactly (1,687.48 and 959.45). Both conventions were tested and are IDENTICAL here because no in-kind is claimed anywhere on the filing: this is the v. 4.20 blank, whose schedules have NO in-kind checkbox column, and — unlike the SAME FILER'S November report, where a 200 gift is declared inline in the name cell and is load-bearing on both sides — no row here carries any in-kind wording. That contrast inside one filer's own cycle is exactly the ADDENDUM G1 rule: in-kind is per FILING, never carried between a filer's reports.
itemized.escalation_note: (1-3) one full-height amount-column crop per schedule page at 900 dpi (pp2, 3, 4), each rendering its rows in band order exactly as recorded plus the empty rows below them; the figures are listed in each frame's measure_note. No cell was in doubt — this is a typed fillable form — and nothing was changed. The mileage-rate check described in recon.expenditures.detail is an additional independent per-row test and it passed on every row.

FORM: modern_boxAF, footer revision 'v. 4.20', the four-column blank with an UNLETTERED close box.

⚠ THE SAME FILER USED TWO DIFFERENT 'v. 4.20' COVERS IN ONE CYCLE — this record and c37543a6 together are the evidence. This April cover offers 'Seven days preceding Convention' among its five report types and carries the JOSH DANIELS masthead; his October cover carries the same 'v. 4.20' footer but offers '30 Days after the Primary Election' instead of Convention, under the AMELIA POWERS GARDNER masthead. So the version footer identifies a print run, not the form's content, and the report-type list must be READ OFF THE PAGE every time.

TWO MASTHEAD VINTAGES INSIDE THIS ONE FILING as well (ADDENDUM J5): pp1, 3 and 4 carry 'Josh Daniels' and pp2 and 5 carry 'Amelia Powers Gardner'.

EIGHT PDF PAGES BUT FIVE REPORT SHEETS, foliated '1 of 5' through '5 of 5' and complete: p1 cover / p2 Schedule A / p3 Schedule B sheet 1 / p4 Schedule B sheet 2 / p5 SUMMARY PAGE / p6 BLANK VERSO / p7 CAMPAIGN FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE CHECKLIST / p8 BLANK VERSO. Every page classified from its own printed header.

A THIRD CHECKLIST IN THIS CHUNK, AND IT MATCHES THE COX 4/1/2022 BINDING EXACTLY: the checklist sits at p7 between two blank versos, and it is the revision WITH the 'HOLD' line and numbered 'Staff Signature #1 / #2' — both copies signed and dated 4/4/22 and 4/4/2022, the same review date as the Cox filing's checklist. So the county reviewed both filings the same day and bound the same checklist revision into both, at the same ordinal. The chunk's checklist tally is now: p7 (Cox 4/1), p5 (Cox 5/9), p7 (this filing), and none in the other five filings.

TWO SELF-LOANS ON THE CONTRIBUTIONS LEDGER, resolved by the ladder and not by the word (ADDENDUM B3) — see recon.contributions.detail. The first is exactly the filing fee he pays the county the same day.

A MILEAGE LOG WITH THE RATE PRINTED IN EVERY ROW: 15 of the 20 expenditure rows are 'Car Miles Deduction' entries whose Purpose cell states 'N miles x .585'. Every one reproduces to the cent, which is an independent per-row check on the amount column — and it is what exposed the single broken row on this filer's NOVEMBER filing (see c37543a6's +0.09 delta). On THIS filing the check is clean on all fifteen.

REDACTION, AND THE CONTRAST WITH HIS OWN NEXT FILING: here the county blacked out the cover's whole address block, the cover signature, and the STREET portion of every donor address, leaving city/state/zip in the clear — so the four contribution rows all carry a real city and state. His 10/31/22 filing is NOT redacted at all, and its address column is the typed word 'Unknown' on every row. One filer, one cycle, two completely different reasons for what an address cell shows: the county's bar here, the filer's placeholder there.

EVERY FIGURE ON THIS FILING CLOSES. Both sides reconcile exactly against three printed anchors each, the summary ladder closes, and the per-row mileage rate closes — the cleanest filing in the chunk.
